title: The Atomiton · Public Tool Library
eligibility_rule: The listed function must have a usable verified no-payment path. Paywalled functions do not qualify.

tools.name: Offline Record Comparator
tools.summary: Turn supplied records into a searchable, sortable and printable comparison view. Keep missing information visible.
tools.function: Compare all rows and fields supplied in a flat JSON dataset, without changing its contents.
tools.audience: People already comparing records while navigating a system, and researchers working alongside them.
tools.research_gap: The supplied records had no mission-specific comparison view. Null, empty and absent fields needed to remain visible.

free_access.path: Open the bundled HTML in a browser. To use new records, run the included standard-library Python compiler.
limits: 2–500 flat records; 2–30 fields; strings or null; up to 512 KB.
Creating a new dataset view requires Python 3.11+. The supplied example opens directly in a browser.

test_results.scope: Search, sorting, source-order restoration, missing fields, hostile strings, inherited property names, print-handler dispatch and script CSP.
test_results.environment: Node.js VM with a DOM fixture; synthetic records. This is not a full browser or user trial.

test_results.scope: All source rows and fields preserved; admitted script, document policy and source digest checked.
test_results.environment: Python standard-library document checks on three synthetic records.

test_results.scope: The standalone compiler recreates the shipped HTML byte for byte without importing Atomiton.
test_results.environment: Python standard library; supplied synthetic records.

limitations: No real-person field trial has been performed.
The tool organises what supplied records say; it does not establish eligibility, current availability or a remedy.
Missing information remains unknown. The comparison gap is partly addressed under the declared technical checks.
adoption_steps: Download and unzip the complete tool bundle.
Open comparison.html for the synthetic working example.
Read GUIDE.txt and inspect the test reports and source.
For your own records, run: python compiler.py your-records.json --out your-comparison.html
Keep the original records and report trial outcomes with the exact tool version.
